profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, who had previously built companies acquired by IXC Communications. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company opened what it described as the largest data center in Texas in Carrollton in 2012, the anchor of the Dallas Fort Worth cluster that this registry row is part of, alongside CyrusOne buildings in nearby Allen, Lewisville, and Collin County. CyrusOne also operates a substantial San Antonio campus and an Austin facility, both long-running Texas markets for the company, though no specific acquisition or opening story for San Antonio or Austin individually was located in available sourcing this session. The company was acquired by ABRY Partners in 2007, purchased by Cincinnati Bell for 525 million dollars in 2010, completed an IPO in 2013, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Among Texas data centers that publish capacity, the CyrusOne San Antonio campus ranks fourth at 36 MW, representing roughly 11 percent of the eight facilities' combined 315 MW total. This single campus could support approximately 900 GPU-dense racks at typical AI training power densities, or 3,600 racks at enterprise densities, yet operators across Texas publish capacity figures for less than 10 percent of mapped facilities, making the true regional total invisible.

The campus holds certifications across payment processing, healthcare, information security, and federal workloads. These qualify it to host regulated data but do not indicate current tenancy. The lack of individual building breakdowns means the 36 MW cannot be attributed to specific structures on the two adjacent parcels.

CyrusOne operates this campus as part of a larger Texas footprint spanning San Antonio, Austin, and the Dallas Fort Worth cluster anchored in Carrollton. The company has traded ownership through acquisition, IPO, and leveraged buyout over two decades, cycling from private to public and back to private in 2022 at a 15 billion dollar valuation. The San Antonio campus has run as a long-standing Texas market presence without a documented opening story in available sources, suggesting stability but limited visibility into when capacity was built or how it has scaled.
